title: A diagram-linked whole distinguishes instrument from endpoint
summary: Test whether a recurring whole refers to an instrument/channel when paired with an incoming edge but to an endpoint when paired with an outgoing destination, rather than one portable object meaning.

design.mechanism: The candidate's role is constrained by independently observed edge direction and terminal geometry.
design.unit: complete whole occurrences at admitted diagram edges with direction and terminal class independently coded
design.contrast: incoming/source-side occurrence versus outgoing/endpoint-side occurrence, matched by panel and register
design.prediction: Neighboring edge geometry separates instrument/channel from endpoint usage reproducibly on held panels; a single object meaning predicts no direction-by-terminal interaction.
design.falsifier: No held geometry interaction or no independent direction/terminal coding falsifies the distinction.
design.scope: admitted visual selectors and direction metadata only; endpoint availability_unknown
design.related: Distinct from owner-conditioned referent and register handoff: tests geometric function, not ownership or presentation transition
